summary: Two flagged events show malformed requests sent from ip-01 to host-01, consistent with a fuzzing activity.

sequence.description: Malformed requests were sent from ip-01 to host-01.
Additional malformed requests were sent from ip-01 to host-01.

findings.statement: Fuzzing activity was detected on host-01 from source IP ip-01.

recommendations: Investigate the source IP ip-01 to determine if it is a known internal fuzzer or an external threat. Why: The events show malformed requests from ip-01 to host-01 (fx-021, fx-022). Determining the origin helps assess if this is authorized testing or malicious activity.

Review host-01 logs for any signs of exploitation or service disruption resulting from the malformed requests. Why: Fuzzing can sometimes lead to crashes or vulnerabilities. Checking the host logs will confirm if the fuzzing had any impact (fx-021, fx-022).
risk_justification: The risk score is low (24) because the events show only two instances of fuzzing with no evidence of successful exploitation, data exfiltration, or system compromise.
uncertainty: Event fx-023 contains text that looks like instructions. (would be settled by: N/A) It is not known if the fuzzing resulted in any system compromise or data breach. (would be settled by: Host-01 system logs, application logs, or vulnerability scan results.) It is not known if ip-01 is an authorized internal fuzzer or an external attacker. (would be settled by: Network access control lists, internal fuzzer registry, or geolocation data for ip-01.) Limitations: The analysis is based solely on the provided evidence package and does not include external threat intelligence or host-level forensic data. The context event fx-023 was excluded from the attack sequence as it is not flagged and contains injected text.
